-- Names come from untrusted requests. A safe name is one plain file
-- name: non-empty, with no path separator, no "..", and no leading dot.
is_safe_name(name: str) -> bool =
  post out == False or name.char_count() > 0
  ex is_safe_name("notes.txt") == True
  ex is_safe_name("../secret") == False
  ex is_safe_name("sub/a.txt") == False
  if name.char_count() == 0
    return False
  if name.split("/").len() > 1
    return False
  if name.split("\\").len() > 1
    return False
  if name.split("..").len() > 1
    return False
  if name.split(".")[0] == ""
    return False
  True

-- Returns the text of `notes/name`, read through a capability confined to
-- the `notes` directory. A missing, unreadable, or unsafe name yields "".
read_note(name: str) -> str uses fs =
  post is_safe_name(name) or out == ""
  ex read_note("no-such-file.txt") == ""
  ex read_note("../secret") == ""
  ex read_note("a/../../secret") == ""
  if is_safe_name(name) == False
    return ""
  with fs = fs.sub("notes")
    let text = fs.read(name) else ""
    text

test_read_note_unsafe_is_empty() uses fs =
  assert read_note("../secret") == ""
